Containers c23, clang16–clang20, gcc13–gcc15 carry R-devel r89629/r89623 (2026-03), predate R_envSymbols header (added r89633) hours, current rlang (>=1.1.7, e.g. 1.3.0) fails compile source (use undeclared identifier 'R_envSymbols'). excluded Linux matrix r-hub rebuilds past r89633. clang21 (healthy newer snapshot r90185) breaks r-hub CRAN binary bit64 links libclang_rt.ubsan_standalone, missing load time -> readr-based parsing fails tests + vignette. Resolved 2026-08-22: source-flag (pkg.platforms = "source" + R_PROFILE) honored — repo table setup-deps shows pak solving source src/contrib — silently defeated r-lib actions/cache. cache key stable (hashes OS/R-version + RHUB repo path + .github/r-depends.rds, bit64’s version 4.8.4 unchanged), poisoned binary bit64.(dated 2026-08-20) restored cache every run; pak’s lockfile_install installs 1-package gap never recompiles cache-restored bit64. (Root cause thus cache restore, platform flag.) Fix refinement 2026-08-22 (run 32561306626): first repair attempt — remove bit64 R_LIBS_USER pak::pkg_install("bit64=?source") — work: step ran (bit64 detected, remove.packages called) pak finished ~1.3s “downloads needed” never recompiled, pak’s solver treats already-installed 4.8.4 satisfying =?source regardless source/binary origin. reliable fix bypass pak’s --date check entirely install CRAN source tarball directly: install.packages(<bit64_4.8.4.tar.gz>, lib=R_LIBS_USER, repos=NULL, type="source"), always compiles container’s native toolchain. clang21-step sits setup-deps run-check; post-run cache step saves repaired library later runs restore good bit64. windows (R-devel) vignette: freshly-installed package passed requireNamespace() yet expose dg_summarise (dg_summary callable) build subprocess. Reproduced across runs 32387247290, 32462190016, 32561358512; neither exists()- get()-based dg hook caught , pointing present--unforceable lazy-load entry reports “callable” yet throws call time. R-devel-Windows-specific; reproducible macOS. Resolved 2026-08-22: dg hook fails closed DATAGOUV_LIVE two decorative chunks set #| error: true (see ), -memory chunks can never abort R CMD build. Note run 32579232283: DATAGOUV_LIVE gate committed, chunk 10 still ran threw R CMD build — gate alone sufficient, either DATAGOUV_LIVE set/leaked Windows build subprocess hook failed fire . error: true hardening environment- independent catches whichever mechanism let chunk run.

title: AGENTS.md
text: vignettes/datagouv.qmd sets knitr::opts_hooks live (DATAGOUV_LIVE=1) dg. dg hook gates two network-free -memory chunks bad environment degrades skip instead failing R CMD build. chunk sets #| dg: <function name> (e.g. dg: dg_summarise) #| error: true, wraps call try() (actual robustness guarantee — see ); hook evaluates chunk DATAGOUV_LIVE=1 "package:datagouv" %% search() named export forces real function — checked get(<fn>, inherits = TRUE) inside tryCatch, exists(). fail closed DATAGOUV_LIVE: pkgdown site render alone sets DATAGOUV_LIVE=1 (see .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml), installed package guaranteed usable; R CMD build/check never set . History: requireNamespace() passed yet export missing; exists(fun, inherits=TRUE) also passed affected Windows/R-devel installs export broken/unforceable lazy-load entry — binding present resolving call time throws find function "dg_summarise" aborts build (run 32462190016). hook therefore upgraded force value get() inside tryCatch, reproduced correctly locally (active binding throws force: exists() said TRUE get()-based hook returned FALSE). run 32561358512 (carried get()-based hook) still aborted chunk 10 — get() returned unforced lazy-load promise without error, hook judged export “callable” subsequent call threw. get()/exists() prediction reliably catches present--unforceable lazy-load entry, hook now gates DATAGOUV_LIVE well. environment gate alone proved insufficient: run 32579232283 (carried DATAGOUV_LIVE-gated hook commit 1130f56) still executed chunk 10 R CMD build aborted — meaning DATAGOUV_LIVE set/leaked Windows build subprocess, hook fire . error: true alone sufficient backstop (run 32594354116, head 9bf4b6f). follow-commit added #| error: true decorative chunks still aborted identically — * creating vignettes ... ERROR, Quitting datagouv.qmd:286-291, find function "dg_summarise". Reproduced locally quarto_render(): knitr’s error option contain normal function-body error, contain unforceable-export hard failure. error raised forcing lazy-load promise call/frame setup — level knitr’s withCallingHandlers around chunk expression never sees — hard-quits regardless error: true. Neither DATAGOUV_LIVE gate get() callability test error: true can stop broken-export chunk executes. robust fix try(), lower-level-contains everything. decorative chunk bodies now wrapped try(<call>) (e.g. try(dg_summarise(...))), base-R catch-converts unforceable-export hard failure printed try-error output instead abort. Verified three ways quarto_render()/R CMD build: (1) healthy install DATAGOUV_LIVE=1 shows real metrics tables (try() swallow correct output); (2) normal R CMD build DATAGOUV_LIVE unset skips chunks builds clean; (3) broken binding hard-quits bare error: true chunk renders completion identical body wrapped try(). removes failure class packaging build keeping examples live website. title: Design proposal — discovery-first refresh
text: dg_list_datasets() currently keeps title/id/description/slug discards resources, students can’t tell whether hit holds real table. Fix: keep resources metadata derive compact availability summary. New columns returned tibble: n_resources — number resources (integer; 0 none). formats — comma-joined, de-duplicated, uppercase formats dataset’s resources, e.g. "CSV, ZIP", "—" none. (Reuse supported_formats().) has_table — logical: TRUE resource directly parseable (non-ZIP supported format). ZIP maybe, shown formats set has_table. Adding makes dg_list_datasets(q = "vélo", n = 20) immediately answer “can actually open?” spending download. Lightest-file preference (pull side). dataset offers table several formats (base file name, different extension), pull path (read_first_parseable_resource()) reduces candidates one smallest advertised filesize (prefer_lightest_file()), dg_pull_dataset()/ dg_refetch() download lighter copy — e.g. data.csv rather heavier data.xlsx twin. Resources distinct names keep declared order, distinct tables never silently swapped. Note: fetch_datasets_page requests single format value per query (API honors one, passing several ). fetch_all_datasets() queries requested format separately unions/de-duplicates dataset id, dg_list_datasets(format = ...) lets caller choose formats keep (defaults full tabular set). resource-level formats still surfaced formats column.

what: Main API vs tabular API: division of labour
title: Design proposal — discovery-first refresh
text: Answering “main API even useful tabular API also serves data?”: yes — main API backbone; tabular API variable-metadata supplement. substitutes. Implications package: dg_list_datasets(q) remains irreplaceable: tabular API keyword search, discovery metadata (dataset interest?) comes main API. educational core rests main API. pull path (read_resource) keeps downloading raw files . preserves full format/coverage (xlsx, json, zip; resources tabular service hasn’t indexed), tabular API guarantee. tabular API’s unique value variable metadata pull time, main API lacks. practice package sources metadata producer’s schema documents schema.data.gouv.fr (see ) rather tabular service’s /profile/ endpoint; tabular service used current implementation. title: Finding, judging and re-fetching French open data with datagouv
text: datagouv small R client public API data.gouv.fr, French government’s open data platform. written specific user mind: student data scientist wants find dataset matches interests, judge whether usable analysis, download , later re-fetch exact table reproducible way. four steps may sound trivial, platform makes harder : Finding. Enumerating “” published datasets means paging tens thousands records. catalog search server-side matches titles descriptions, free-form often uninformative. Judging. tabular API provides human-readable variable descriptions. actual descriptions live separate schema documents schema.data.gouv.fr; data.gouv.fr attaches pointer (name / url) resource. Without resolving pointer, tell whether column really means assume. Downloading. Catalog titles even ordering change time, script reaches dataset “title” fragile. want address always resolves table. datagouv addresses four. functions organised around workflow: approach mirrors several US cities propose (e.g. nycOpenData New York), tailored data.gouv.fr API.

text: dg_pull_dataset() downloads first parseable tabular resource dataset returns single tibble: things know pulling: Supported formats csv, csv.gz, xls, xlsx, parquet, tsv, txt json. ZIP resource unpacked first parseable file returned default; all_files = TRUE keeps every contained file one formats named list — one element per file. delimiter CSV/TXT resources auto-detected (comma, semicolon, tab, pipe, …), standard European-style files (semicolon / decimal-comma) handled without configuration. Declared formats always accurate, candidate may fail parse (e.g. json resource actually serves API metadata document). dg_pull_dataset() skips non-parseable resources falls back next tabular one instead erroring. dataset offers table several formats (file name, different extension, e.g. data.csv vs data.xlsx), lightest advertised file downloaded pull small possible; resources distinct names keep declared order. Every returned table carries stable, unique address id attribute, readable dg_table_id().

code: # The call is wrapped in try() as a low-level backstop: neither knitr's # `error: true` option nor the DATAGOUV_LIVE/get() gate can contain a # present-but-unforceable lazy-load export (the Windows/R-devel failure, # see AGENTS.md), whereas try() degrades even that hard failure to printed # output instead of aborting R CMD build/check. try(dg_summary(iris, name = "iris")) # A tibble: 1 × 7   dataset size_kb n_vars n_numeric n_non_numeric n_rows prop_missing   <chr>     <dbl>  <int>     <int>         <int>  <int>        <dbl> 1 iris       7.09      5         4             1    150            0 # In-memory tables — no network needed #| dg: dg_summarise #| error: true try(dg_summarise(datasets = list(iris = iris, mtcars = mtcars))) # A tibble: 2 × 7   dataset size_kb n_vars n_numeric n_non_numeric n_rows prop_missing * <chr>     <dbl>  <int>     <int>         <int>  <int>        <dbl> 1 iris       7.09      5         4             1    150            0 2 mtcars     7.04     11        11             0     32            0

title: List datasets available on data.gouv.fr — dg_list_datasets
text: q Optional full-text search query. given, datasets matching q returned (API performs search). Defaults NULL, meaning filtering. n Maximum number datasets return. Defaults 1000. Set Inf retrieve everything (whole catalog). format Optional character vector resource formats keep. given, datasets least one resource one formats returned; requested format queried server-side results combined. Defaults full set officially tabular formats (csv, csv.gz, xls, xlsx, parquet). schema_only Whether keep datasets declare data schema (see has_schema). Defaults FALSE.

title: List datasets available on data.gouv.fr — dg_list_datasets
text: tibble::tibble() one row per matching dataset columns title, id, description, slug, n_resources, formats, has_table has_schema. id column holds stable, unique dataset identifier used address dataset dg_pull_dataset(). n_resources number files/resources dataset, formats lists distinct file formats found among , has_table indicates whether least one resource format can parsed table package, has_schema indicates whether least one resource carries pointer declared data schema (whose per-variable documentation exposed dg_schema()).

title: List datasets available on data.gouv.fr — dg_list_datasets
text: Fetching every dataset platform means paging tens thousands records hundreds HTTP requests slow fragile, default deliberately bounded. Set n = Inf return titles regardless count.
